I thought that Taco Bell Bold and Creamy Spicy Ranchero Sauce had a lot of potential. After all, a number of Taco Bell restaurant menu offerings are quite good, even if not necessarily exceptional.

Alas, I was disappointed; sorely disappointed, in fact. Let's start with nutritional information. A two tablespoon serving--- a fairly large serving, actually--- is 110 calories. That's quite a bit, but a smaller serving could control this. The issue is that of these 110 calories, a whopping 100 of them are from fat. That's hardly a healthy makeup.

What about flavor? The sauce was creamy in consistency, but it was not creamy in taste; for that matter, neither was it bold or spicy. Our daughter described it as "taco seasoning mixed with lard." That is perhaps a bit harsh as there is no lard in the product, but nevertheless the sauce does have a fatty mouth feel and very little flavor. We tried it on a mixed salad (with onions, etc., to ensure that it would not be over-powered); we also tried it on tortilla chips and cooked ground beef. The results were all the same. There was little flavor and the sauce made the food taste and feel fatty.

Though I wanted to like the sauce, I have to say that based on our experience with it, I definitely can't recommend it. It is unhealthy and lacking in flavor, and generally detracts from the food it was intended to enhance.

Full disclosure: I really have to point out that the review sample I received was a few days beyond the "best used by" date. Although this wasn't exactly clever marketing to send your expired stock to your reviewers, I doubt if the product had deteriorated much if at all. Still, I mention this because it could have conceivably had an effect, and if you choose to buy the product, by all means be sure you have fresh stock.

I've been waiting for ages for this product to show up on Amazon so that I can review it. I've been enjoying Mrs. Renfro's Mango Habanero salsa for quite a while, enjoying its fantastic heat/sweet ratio, and just wishing it was chunkier and a bit hotter. Then along comes this stuff. They must have been listening!

I'm pretty sure this is the hottest salsa Mrs. Renfro's offers, and I think it's the perfect level for those of us who really enjoy some heat with our salsa but don't have a hot foods shoppe nearby. I'll take this opportunity to kvetch that I have seen some reviews out there--video reviews--of people opening a jar of this stuff, dipping the corner of a chip in it, eating the whole chip, and going, 'Oh, it's not that hot.'

Yeah, duh. It's not hot sauce, people. It's SALSA. It's meant to be enjoyed in moderate SCOOPS, not in tiny little dollops like Blair's Sudden Death (excellent, btw). SCOOP the stuff onto a chip the way you're meant to, and have yourself about five chips in this manner. Now stop. ... Yeah, I *thought* you'd be reaching for the tissues. Welcome to chips and salsa. That's how you eat them.

Onward: This salsa has a great texture--it could be chunkier, it's true (all the Mrs. Renfro's salsas have this issue), but it's chunkier than many of their others, and it's still thick enough to stick to the chip.

The flavour is almost a head-scratcher. When you get that first bite, right before the heat smacks you across the face, there's this moment of, 'Ooh. Hey. What's that?' Some have called it curry-like, others chili-like (not as in pepper, but as in a pot of chili). I realize this makes me a bad reviewer, but I'm honestly not sure *what* it is. I think it's part garlic, part roasted tomatoes, and part... part... oh, I don't know. Liquid deliciousness? Yeah, that sounds right.

Upon first bite, this salsa became my current favourite. (I'd spell out the happy moan I let loose when I first tried it, but this is a family site.) In the course of a month, I have finished four jars of it. That is not an exaggeration. I have been driven to unexpectedly have chips and salsa for dinner more times than a person should (should they ever?) for the love of this salsa.

My local grocery put it on sale. Oh, bad move, people. I cleared them out. Thank the chili gods that they restocked.

I have tried a lot of salsa in my life. Most of the really good spicy stuff is only available in chilihead specialty shoppes or online with massive shipping charges (but hey, the stuff is heavy). To my knowledge, this is the hottest salsa (I repeat: NOT HOT SAUCE) that you can find in a regular grocery store.

I've already recommended it to all my friends who enjoy hot foods or have people in their family who do so. Now I recommend it to you. Enjoy it! I know I do.

Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty Ultra Shea Cleanse & Nourish Shampoo is a nice shampoo. I've got very, very dry and frizzy hair, so I usually avoid products with sodium lauryl sulfate and sodium laureth sulfate. This shampoo has sodium laureth sulfate, but when I used it with its accompanying Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty Ultra Shea Smooth & Nourish Conditioner, my hair emerged silky (though still frizzy since the beauty industry has yet to invent a flat iron in a bottle).

I usually use $20 per bottle shampoo and matching conditioner from my local salon in attempts to make my hair behave. I'm not going to stop using those in favor of this more economical shampoo due to the presence of sodium laureth sulfate. But I'm going to add this one in about once a month for a little variety and as a way to stretch my expensive shampoo out. Every little bit helps in budgeting!

A few bonuses: this product smells fantastic and the bottle design that dispenses shampoo from the bottom is terrific!

As a French Roast fan, I bought this brand of K-cup with high expectations, considering the name attached to it. I was disappointed. It has a hearty aroma and full-bodied flavor but leaves a bitter aftertaste.

If you're a lover of the more robust roasts, I would recommend trying the Coffee People Kona Blend Island Style, Extra Bold K-Cups for Keurig Brewers (Pack of 50) instead. It is a smooth blend with none of the bitterness that delivers that kick you're likely looking for.

I was very skeptical that this would taste as good as the other reviewers said, but it was on sale so I figured I'd give it a try. My 5-yr-old son LOVES scones. Well, not only does it taste great, but it's ridiculously easy to make and my son was able to help me. In addition, my family comes from England so I've had my fair share of all sorts of scones. I have to say these taste pretty authentic. After they were done I wished I'd had clotted cream to go with. And organic to boot, what a find!

Also, being a mom who has to juggle, and never finding a recipe I didn't have to tweak, I found an even easier way to make them than the instructions on the box. Using 2 boxes I dumped the mixes directly into a disposable foil 1/2 size lasagna pan. Then I put in a full stick of butter that was room temp. I forked it till the dough was little lumps. I didn't add a flavor because I wanted to see what "original" was like. (Great.) Then I put in a cup of milk and forked it around till it was smooth dough. There was still some dry mix at the bottom of the pan so I added the couple of tablespoons of milk. Then, I got my hands in there and it wasn't too difficult to pick up the stray bits till the pan was clean and the dough was a ball. Then I smoothed out the dough evenly in the pan. Then I took a knife and scored it in quarters till I had 16 triangles. Baked it and done.

Mind you, I must say that my "easy" way of doing it is only if you don't mind not having the crusty edges on each triangle, the mark of a "real" scone I suppose. To me, I'd rather save the time, the dishes, and it tastes the same, delicious!
